title: Purdue Model Attack Paths
description: Interactive SVG of the Purdue model levels (5 down to 0) with the IT/OT boundary highlighted and three historical ICS attack paths overlaid - Stuxnet, Colonial Pipeline, and Oldsmar - each annotated with the control that failed.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

educational.topic: Industrial control systems, the Purdue model, and the IT/OT boundary
learningObjectives: Identify the six Purdue levels and locate the IT/OT boundary.
Trace three real ICS attacks through the Purdue levels.
Name the specific control that failed in each historical attack.
educational.prerequisites: Awareness that operational technology controls physical processes.

pedagogical.modelType: interactive layered infographic with attack overlays
pedagogical.assessment: Discussion questions in the lesson plan ask students to map a new intrusion onto the levels and propose the missing control.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing an air gap is sufficient to protect OT (Stuxnet crossed via USB).
Assuming an attacker must reach Level 0 to cause operational impact (Colonial caused a shutdown from IT).
